asr.full_text: Hey guys and welcome to another episode of Zach's Credit Card Guide. Today we are talking about a business card from Wells Fargo that seems to fly under the radar and nobody really talks about. But it is one that you need to check out. If you are new to the channel we do a lot of credit card topics, card reviews and redemptions so make sure to hit that subscribe button but let's get started. So guys I wanted to talk to you real quick about the newest card to my wallet and that is the Business Platinum from Wells Fargo. So, first, we'll talk about some of the card details. Now, the reward system is a little bit unique in that you can pick what you want. Either cashback or reward points. Now, you choose this when you apply for the card so you can't switch back and forth, but you can choose either path that you like. Now, both paths are relatively simple. The cashback option is just one and a half percent, like a lot of other cards out there. And then if you go for points, it's just one point per dollar. Now, with points, if you spend more than $1,000 in a billing cycle, they will give you 1,000 extra bonus points. Now, this card does come with a 0% intro APR for the first nine months. Now, again, on this channel, I always recommend paying off your entire bill in full every single month. Never carry a balance because that can lead to paying interest and that negates this entire hobby. But again, this is 0% for nine months. So if you have a purchase that you want to finance for that period, you can do that. Now, what is really cool about this card is that it has no annual fee and no foreign transaction fee. Those two don't normally pair up together in the credit card world. Now, it is pretty light on benefits. If you choose points, you can redeem those for the usual suspects, gift cards, some merchandise, airline tickets, stuff like that. Now, I do believe with the airline tickets, if you choose points and go the Wells Fargo route, I do believe that they charge fees to redeem for tickets. So, something to keep in mind, but I think a lot of people who are into this hobby, and if you stumbled across this video, this is probably not going to become your everyday card, but again, it is something to keep in mind. Now, it has some of the basic benefits. It has purchase protection, which usually covers your purchases from theft and damage for the first 90 days. And it does have extended warranty as well. Now, what I was surprised to read when I was looking through the Terms and Conditions pamphlet is that it does have rental coverage, but the terms are fairly clear. Again, this is a business card, so it has primary rental coverage, which again is very rare, especially for a no annual fee card. The only other card I can think of off the top of my head is the Sapphire Reserve, which is a $450 annual fee personal card from Chase. That has primary rental coverage as well and what that means really briefly is that when you rent a car They always try to talk you into getting their insurance a lot of credit cards have Secondary rental coverage, which basically means you have to go to your insurance first And if for some reason they don't pay out, then this insurance kicks in. What this is, is primary. So you can just rent a car and use your credit card and that's your insurance. You don't have to buy it from the rental car company. It doesn't touch your personal insurance. It just goes through the credit card. Now, there are some terms and conditions in this particular one. It's not valid in certain countries and everything else. We're not going to get into that. But what is interesting is that this is primary rental coverage but it does say explicitly that the trip has to be for business purposes. Again, this is a business card. Now, at insurance they usually ask for verification and things like that. Especially, when they're trying to see if coverage is going to apply. So, if you take a personal trip to Vegas for the weekend, get in a car, and wreck it, they might ask to see proof that you were on a business trip so I would be very cautious with that now it does say that it will cover you in a rental car for a personal trip but it's secondary so again it might go to your personal insurance first and everything else so I tell you all that just to let you know the benefit is there but again please read the terms and conditions before relying on it and finally the part you've all been waiting for the bonus. Now again this is a no annual fee card. The option for cash back is a five hundred dollar bonus. If you use points it's fifty thousand points and they are both, again whichever route you pick, for three thousand dollars in the first three months. Now a really cool thing about this card is they allow a degree of freedom when designing the card. They're going to send you the regular one in the mail, which looks like this but then if you want to go into the design studio, you can do all sorts of stuff, they have a bunch of stock images but you can also upload like a company logo or something which is what I did. And then it looks really custom and actually pretty professional too coz again it is a business card. So I do like that that feature a lot of credit card companies will only allow you to use like images very few of them will let you put text or logos or anything like that so it is really cool that this wells fargo card lets you do that so what do i think about the card again i just added this to my wallet i'm working on the minimum spread right now i'm using the cash back bonus to buy an awesome 4k monitor that i just got today and actually i will be reviewing it on my cross channel slick reviews so head over and check that out too but again the cash back bonus is pretty sweet and this is a no annual fee card so this is a prime candidate to pick up if you want a quick cash back bonus. Again, $500. That is pretty high, especially for a no annual fee card. The only other one I've ever come across that has a bonus of that high level is the Ink Cash or something like that from Chase. It is fine to get the bonus and then just put it in a sock drawer because again, it has no annual fee, so there's never really a reason to ever close it. The only thing I didn't care for is that you have to be a wells fargo customer you have to have a checking account or something with them for a year or more before they'll let you apply for this online i actually had to go in branch like it's 1992 and apply for this card in person i had to sit down with somebody and talk to them about my business and everything else before they would even start filling out the application. So, this is not necessarily one of those cards to apply for, at least in branch, if you have a business, okay? So, if you can actually justify something and show that you've been doing some sort of activity and making money from it, if you can justify it, again, if you have to go in branch, then that's fine. Just go ahead and do that that's what I did I didn't have any issues but I know some people in this hobby again have a business and unless you're a really smooth talker or something like that I don't know how you're gonna do so anyway guys real quick video this week just wanted to tell you about this card again easy prime awesome sign up bonus no fee, no reason not to pick it up My question for you guys is Have you heard of this card before? Do you already have it? What do you think about it? Let me know down in the comments But if you guys have any other comments or questions Please do leave them down below I try to get to every single one Find me on social media so you can stay in touch But most importantly guys Hit that subscribe button So you don't miss any future videos That's all I've got for you this time guys. See at the next one!
